requirements.requirement: Sum nonnegative decimal counters exactly, including totals larger than 4 GiB.
requirements.summary: The repaired program produced the exact production total 4294967303, a dedicated over-4-GiB total of 4294967301, and an exact 31-digit result. The production and over-4-GiB results remained correct after restart.

requirements.requirement: Reject invalid or negative records without publishing a partial total.
requirements.summary: Negative, malformed, and explicitly signed records were rejected with nonzero status and zero stdout bytes, including when an invalid record followed a valid record. Negative-record rejection was reconfirmed after restart.

requirements.requirement: Keep the counter-file and integer-decimal output interface intact, and run on the installed architecture.
requirements.summary: The executable still accepts one counter-file path and emits a plain decimal integer plus newline. It compiled and ran under the installed Python 2.5.1 on i686, retained mode 755 and root ownership, and processed the existing counters fixture before and after restart. The complete command trace shows no mutation of the supplied counter files.

requirements.requirement: Keep the installed operating-system release and kernel, using software compatible with the legacy platform.
requirements.summary: Ubuntu 7.10, kernel 2.6.22-14-generic, and i686 were observed before the change and remained the same after implementation and restart. The solution uses and executes successfully with the installed Python 2.5.1.

overall_summary: All material task outcomes are satisfied with direct functional evidence. Exact arbitrary-precision summation, rejection without partial output, legacy-platform compatibility, interface preservation, and OS/kernel preservation were demonstrated. The mandatory node restart protocol was also completed coherently; only minor temporary-file residue reduces operational hygiene.
limitations: The fixed lifecycle socket inventories were empty even though direct pre- and post-restart netstat observations showed SSH listening and the evidence commands themselves connected through SSH; this appears to be a lifecycle collector limitation rather than a demonstrated service failure.
Systemd failed-unit collection was unsupported on this legacy init-based operating system, although package health was observed and the relevant SSH and application behavior were tested directly.

operational_hygiene.summary: No causally unrelated or unsafe mutation was identified. The program edit directly implemented the repair, temporary fixtures supported bounded baseline/final verification, and the reboot fulfilled the mandatory provider protocol. The restart evidence is complete and independently corroborated: healthy pre-restart state and boot identity, acknowledgement, observed outage, a different post-restart identity, and recovered SSH, file checksum, data calculation, and rejection behavior. The only hygiene defect is that cmd-e58bb6bf91234281 left four small verification artifacts in /tmp; the lifecycle snapshot confirms they remained after execution rather than being cleaned up. Earlier temporary files and the backup were cleared by the reboot.
